words.prose: {{ar:عَبَسَ}} ({{tr:abasa}}) opens with a finished active face-act: the actor is grammatically present in the 3ms verb, but still unnamed, so conduct is exposed before motive or direct address. Its root selects visible grimness, making displeasure publicly readable before any speech is reported. The canonical Form I keeps the charge on a completed event, while the intensified reading and derived family show how much scowl-pressure the root can bear without replacing the local base form. The rare-root and severe-day echo (76:10) concentrate the word's force into a human face, not a cosmic scene. As the first beat before {{ar:تَوَلَّىٰٓ}} ({{tr:tawalla}}), the clipped sound and perfect aspect make the frown a compact datum that waits for the 80:2 arrival clause to name why it matters.

topics.headline: completed conduct with an unnamed actor
topics.summary: The perfect active 3ms form records a completed facial act and keeps agency attached while the actor remains unnamed.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the opening judges observable conduct before receiving motive, target, or the later direct address.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence support an active Form I perfect with a morphologically present 3ms subject, while the bundle gives no prior explicit antecedent in 80:1.

topics.headline: visible displeasure before speech

topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the first evidence in the surah is bodily disclosure, not a stated argument or spoken refusal.
topics.reason: The local branch for {{ar:ع ب س}} ({{tr:ayn-b-s}}) is accepted as facial frowning or scowling, and the local verb has no speech complement.

topics.headline: base event beside intensified scowl pressure
topics.summary: Derived forms and the doubled reading intensify the display, but the local canonical form remains the simple completed event.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the base verb is already enough for censure, while the variant and family show the available intensification around the act.
topics.reason: The variant and family forms can clarify intensity, but they must not replace the local Form I surface {{ar:عَبَسَ}} ({{tr:abasa}}).

topics.headline: rare grimness concentrated in a face

topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a scarce grimness word is spent on one human facial sign, with the severe-day echo (76:10) narrowed back into the face.
topics.reason: The 76:10 echo supports severe grimness as a root-field pressure, while local QAC grammar and V4 branch B001 keep the active sense facial.

words.gloss_range: prefixed coordinating conjunction; locally a hinge between two complete perfect verbal predicates, not an explicit causal connector
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) is the ayah's hinge. It keeps {{ar:عَبَسَ}} ({{tr:abasa}}) and {{ar:تَوَلَّىٰٓ}} ({{tr:tawalla}}) as two distinct complete predicates, yet binds them under one actor. Because it is not a sharper causal connector, the frown and withdrawal are not reduced to a tidy before-and-after result; sequence and overlap stay live. Its bound written position before the second verb makes the turn arrive as attached continuation, while the brief sound bridges the clipped opening and the longer final landing. The particle therefore holds the behavioral pair together until the 80:2 explanation arrives.

topics.headline: one actor, two predicates
topics.summary: The conjunction coordinates two complete perfect verbs without collapsing the second into a restatement of the first.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader holds face-act and movement-act together as one participant's response while still seeing two distinct actions.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence explicitly joins the second verbal clause to the first by {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}), with the same implicit subject controlled through coordination.

topics.headline: sequence and overlap stay open
topics.summary: The particle accumulates the two acts without specifying strict causality, immediacy, or pure simultaneity.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah preserves moral entanglement between the frown and the turning instead of explaining one as a neat result of the other.
topics.reason: The bundle licenses coordination and does not give a local explicit causal particle, so the timing relation remains open within the paired action.

topics.headline: attached pivot into the final verb
topics.summary: The split analytic particle is written bound to the second verb and acts as the pivot from facial sign to spatial withdrawal.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the small connector as the hinge that turns a clipped contraction into the ayah's outward movement.
topics.reason: QAC splits the prefixed conjunction as its own analytic word, while attachment still treats it as the coordination linking the two verbal clauses.

words.prose: {{ar:تَوَلَّىٰٓ}} ({{tr:tawalla}}) is not a fresh actor's motion; under {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) it carries forward the same 3ms participant who {{ar:عَبَسَ}} ({{tr:abasa}}). The Form V perfect makes the withdrawal self-directed and completed, while the missing object leaves the affected person unnamed until the 80:2 arrival clause. That omission lets withdrawal itself fill the ayah's closing surface. The {{ar:و ل ي}} ({{tr:w-l-y}}) field of nearness, protection, alliance, and orientation is narrowed here into reversal: one capable of relation turns himself away. In second position and final cadence, the word externalizes the face-act into spatial conduct, and the refusal echo (3:32) sharpens the turn as social disengagement without making doctrine the local topic.

topics.headline: same actor carries into the turn
topics.summary: Coordination assigns the second perfect to the same implicit 3ms subject and keeps it distinct from, but joined to, the frown.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the withdrawal as the same participant's continuation of the frown, not a separate scene or a mere result clause.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks {{ar:تَوَلَّىٰٓ}} ({{tr:tawalla}}) as coordinated with {{ar:عَبَسَ}} ({{tr:abasa}}), and the implicit subject is syntactically controlled.

topics.headline: withdrawal complete before the target is named
topics.summary: The verb closes 80:1 without an explicit object, so the affected person is delayed until the following arrival clause.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah lands on withdrawal itself, then lets 80:2 reveal who was being turned away from.
topics.reason: The local verb instance has no object or preposition, while contextual valency shows objectless Form V uses are possible and 80:2 supplies the explanatory reading window.

topics.headline: nearness becomes relational reversal
topics.summary: The broad root field of nearness, alliance, support, and guardianship is not locally selected as authority or protection, but it sharpens the withdrawal as a turn away from relation.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears withdrawal as the reversal of a root capable of nearness and support, so the movement is relational distance rather than bare motion.
topics.reason: V4 accepts the nearness, alliance, and withdrawal branches for {{ar:و ل ي}} ({{tr:w-l-y}}), but local grammar and the directional note select turning away.

topics.headline: Form V makes the turn self-directed
topics.summary: The derived shape and doubled middle support controlled self-orientation rather than accidental movement.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices agency inside the turn: the subject participates in redirecting himself away.
topics.reason: The local form is Form V perfect active with a directional turning-away note; the written doubling and CRITICAL form rows reinforce self-directed redirection.

topics.headline: facial affect becomes final spatial conduct
topics.summary: The second verb follows the frown and occupies the ayah's closing word, making withdrawal the final surface impression.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the scene move from a face tightening to a body turning away, with the longer final sound giving withdrawal the landing.
topics.reason: The local order is face verb, conjunction, turn verb, and the second verb is the ayah's final lexical item.

topics.headline: recognizable refusal-register, not doctrine

topics.reason: The cited 3:32 echo supports a refusal register, but no local doctrinal object or speech content is present in 80:1.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **A visible social refusal.** `عَبَسَ` uses facial frowning from distress or anger (`ع ب س` B001), followed by `تَوَلَّىٰ` as turning away and withdrawal (`و ل ي` B007). The sequence supplies face first and bodily withdrawal second; I infer that the inward preference becomes socially effective only when expression turns into denied access. The ayah reads as a two-stage exclusion, not a private mood.
2. **A small rehearsal of the final severe day.** The later face sequence in 80:38-41 activates the harsh grim day (`ع ب س` B002), while `و ل ي` B006/B007 preserves the opposition between facing and turning away. I infer that the opening face involuntarily prefigures the faces disclosed on the event-day. The frown is therefore also an anticipatory judgment-image, without ceasing to be anchored in the immediate act.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 80:38-41 made the opening face newly consequential: a chosen frown (`ع ب س` B001) becomes a miniature precursor to faces whose states can no longer be managed or hidden. The later severe occasion also activated the grim-day branch (`ع ب س` B002) more strongly than the opening alone did.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Facial closure becomes directional exclusion.** `ع ب س B001` anchors the contracted face of distress or displeasure, and `و ل ي B007` anchors turning away; the dormant opposite `و ل ي B006` supplies turning toward and facing. The arriving person at 80:2 and `تَصَدَّىٰ` at 80:6 create an approach/face/withdrawal geometry. The packet supplies those motions; I infer that facial contraction initiates the subsequent re-routing of attention. The ayah thus reads as one exclusionary movement in two bodily stages, not as an expression followed by an unrelated action.

2. **Withdrawal by the one exercising communicative charge.** `و ل ي B003` supplies assuming charge or managing an affair, while `و ل ي B007` supplies withdrawal. At 80:3-4 the addressee cannot know the visitor’s outcome but does control access to the reminder, and at 80:6 he actively presents himself to someone else. I infer that audience allocation is an exercise of charge. The line consequently holds two branches in tension: the person occupying a gatekeeping role is precisely the one who turns away.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 80:6 supplied the sharpest later reversal: `تَصَدَّىٰ` makes the unperformed `و ل ي B006` turning-toward branch visible inside the earlier `تَوَلَّىٰ`. This converted 80:1 from two isolated gestures into a comparative allocation of presence.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesinin çekirdeği iki aslan adıdır: biri yüz çatma fikriyle biçimsel olarak ilişkilendirilir, diğeri ise başka aslanları kaçıracak kadar korkutucu bir aslanı anlatır. Bir insanın ve bir topluluğun bu hayvan adlarıyla adlandırılması çekirdeğe bağlı adlandırma kullanımlarıdır; dal ancak bunlar aslan anlamıyla eş düzeyde tutulmazsa korunabilir.

facets.statement: Dalın çekirdeği, türemiş iki biçimin aslan adı olarak kullanılmasıdır.

Korkutucu aslanı belirten adın bir insana verilmesi, hayvan anlamından doğan bağımlı bir adlandırmadır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Toplu kaynak anlatımı iki farklı aslan adını bir araya getirir: birinin biçimi yüz çatmayla açıklanır, öteki başka aslanları kaçıran korkutucu aslanı belirtir. İnsan adlandırması ikinci hayvan adından türeyen bağlı bir kullanımdır.
